name: Sass
summary: CSS preprocessor whose best ideas the platform has since absorbed.
what_it_is: A CSS preprocessor adding variables, nesting, mixins, functions, partials and imports, compiled to plain CSS. The SCSS syntax is a superset of CSS, so any valid stylesheet is already valid SCSS.
why_it_matters: Sass is still in wide production use and remains a perfectly reasonable choice — but the ground shifted underneath it. Native custom properties, native nesting and modern layout removed the reasons most people originally reached for it, and its own @import was deprecated in favour of @use. What still has no native equivalent is mixins and compile-time logic. If Sass is where your styling knowledge stopped, the useful question is not whether to abandon it, but which of its features you are still running a build step for when the browser now does them natively.
suitable_for: Existing codebases with substantial Sass already written
Design systems that genuinely need mixins and compile-time logic
Teams wanting partials and file organisation without a bundler-driven approach
not_suitable_for: New projects wanting only variables and nesting, which CSS now provides natively
Projects trying to remove build steps from their styling pipeline
Teams who would be better served by a shared token scale than by a preprocessor
verifiable_facts: Actively maintained. The documentation records that @import is deprecated in favour of @use.
editorial_interpretation: That native CSS has absorbed most of what people reached for it to do.
Classification as established rather than declining.
context_dependent_guidance: Suitable: Existing codebases with substantial Sass already written
Suitable: Design systems that genuinely need mixins and compile-time logic
Suitable: Teams wanting partials and file organisation without a bundler-driven approach
Unsuitable: New projects wanting only variables and nesting, which CSS now provides natively
Unsuitable: Projects trying to remove build steps from their styling pipeline

evidence_gaps: No evidence about how much Sass usage is legacy maintenance versus new authoring.
wrong_if: A reviewer judges the deprecation of @import and the growth of native CSS nesting to make "declining" the more honest classification.
